notes: Runner: Claude Code remote, GitHub MCP as masenf (verified via get_me). api.github.com unreachable from the sandbox; head SHAs from anonymous git ls-remote.

Listing: 88 rows matched the search open-counter (88) exactly, no mid-scrape reconciliation needed this run. 61 non-draft measured against main 8853e145 (up from 2fc45ed5 yesterday, +3 merges, 0 new PRs opened: 91 - 3 = 88 reconciles exactly).

Merge-box refresh strategy: compared today's listing.updated_at against yesterday's per PR. 56 of 61 non-draft PRs were byte-identical in updated_at, meaning nothing (no push, comment, review, or label) touched them since yesterday's fetch — their prstate was carried forward with two things always recomputed fresh: mergeable/conflicting_files via a new `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's main (cheap, no API cost, and the only way a PR's merge box can change without its own updated_at moving), and days_waiting_on_maintainer against today's date. As a integrity check, all 25 of those 56 whose checks were non-green yesterday had their check-runs re-fetched directly via the API today; every one matched yesterday's recorded state exactly (same run IDs, same conclusions). The remaining 5 PRs with real activity (#7040, #6917, #7033, #7035, #7036) got a full fresh fetch: get, get_reviews, get_review_comments, get_check_runs, get_comments.

The merge-tree conflict script had a regex bug on its first pass today (required a trailing period that git's 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in <path>' message doesn't have), which silently produced empty file lists for 5 PRs including the three newly-conflicting otel PRs. Caught by inspecting one PR's raw merge-tree output by hand before writing conflicting_files into prstate; fixed and the full pass re-run.
The MCP get does not expose the mergeable boolean; mergeable is derived from mergeable_state (dirty = CONFLICTING, otherwise MERGEABLE) for the 5 freshly-fetched PRs, same as yesterday.
Scoring per references/scoring.md. #7035 and #7006 dropped out of yesterday's top15 as new information made them look worse (real bugs found; new conflict), not because of any ranking-formula change.
